segments.he: ר' שמשון ז"ל מאומן נכד רבינו ז"ל בא פעם אחת לבארדיטשוב ואז הי' שם א' מאנש"ש ר' שמשון מבארדיטשוב והי' אז מלמד (והוא קירב את ר' שמואל העשיל ז"ל שעשה בסיביר) והוא נפטר בירושלים ומקום מנוחתו על הר הזיתים. והיו עוסקים ביחד בעבודת השם ופתאום באמצע הסתכל על השעון כאומר שאין לו זמן ושאל אותו הר' שמשון מאומן מדוע אין לו זמן עכשיו הלא עכשיו אין הזמן של הלמוד בפחדר. והשיב לו שמוכרח לילך להזמן של למחות א"ע "עס מיז דיא צייט ואס ער דארץ זיך גיין אוס קרעחצין" ושאל אותו פירוש הדברים וביאר לו שכאשר הוא עני ואביון וכשבא לביתו וזוגתו מתחלת לתבוע מתאנחת אין לו עצה אחרת כי אם לעזור לה להתאנח (איהר ציא העלפין קרעחצין) כי אם יראה לנגדה אז פנים שמחים תכבד אותו כדבעי וע"כ עוזר לה להתאנח ובזה מניח דעתה וע"כ יש לו שיעור בכל יום לילך לעזור לה להתאנח וע"כ אין לו זמן.
segments.en:
Rabbainu said: "I would want to have my gathering in Eretz Yisroel." "Ikh volt gevolt hobn maynem a kibutz in Eretz Yisroel."

And Rabbainu said he envied Reb Yoskel — a very simple man who had a very large and thick siddur with all the old supplications and all the yotzros for every Shabbos of the year. His custom was to go to the house of study every day with his thick siddur and not to move from there until he had begun from the beginning: Modeh Ani — and recited everything in order — even all the Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur prayers, Pesach, Sukkos, all the blessings, the shofar blessings, Bircas HaMazon, wedding blessings, circumcision blessings, and so forth — all of it until the end — finishing the entire siddur from page to page every day. And Rabbainu envied him — for simplicity is highest of all.

[I heard a similar story about the Ba'al Shem Tov — who also envied such a simple man in his day, and said that every time he recited the prayers and psalms for Pesach, a Pesach rectification was made in the Heavens above, and so for Shavuos, and so forth. And also the well-known story of the Bread of the Presence in the time of the Ari: a simple man heard the sermon of the great Rav about the great rectifications that were achieved during the time of the Temple through the Bread of the Presence, and asked him what it was and how it was made. The Rav told him the full procedure of its making. He went home and agreed with his wife to make Bread of the Presence every week — to knead it through thirteen siftings and to bring it in the Holy Ark every Friday and beseech Hashem to eat it and that it should be pleasing and sweet to Him. And the shammes would find it and think it had been left for him, and eat it for Shabbos. When he came later and did not find it, he thought Hashem had eaten it, and was greatly joyful. And so it went on for a long time. Once the man came to the house of study with his bread and went straight to the Holy Ark — and did not see that the Rav was there — and spoke his usual requests to Hashem to eat the bread. The Rav overheard and rebuked him: "Fool! Does G-d eat?" He asked who then was eating it, and learned it was the shammes. He said: "Then I will do teshuvah." The Rav was repeating the sermon he was to give the next Shabbos. The Ari sent for him — that he should command his household, for at the hour when he was to give the sermon he would die, G-d preserve us, because he had shattered the delight of Hashem. For from that simple man Hashem had received as much delight as from the Bread of the Presence in the Temple.]
